findings.detail: Decision 2 defers Kafka/Redis/ClickHouse, but no Notion document describes how windowed aggregates, calendar accumulators, late-event re-evaluation or simulation work on Postgres alone; the infrastructure doc only says all transactions stay in Postgres at T1. Sentinel's per-ingest scan proves the modular-monolith path works functionally but does not scale to 6-month windows or 500 tx/s, and gives no simulation path.
findings.design_impact: The TM sub-spec must define the Postgres implementation of §4.2: a `txn_bucket(tenant, key_kind, key, aggregate_id, bucket_start, value)` table updated in the ingest transaction (hourly ≤ 7 d, daily ≤ 6 m, calendar-period rows), aggregates read by summing buckets, re-evaluation for late events within 7 days, and a simulation runner over the partitioned transaction table. Sync decisions (T2) can be served from the same table with an index until Redis arrives.
findings.suggested_resolution: Specify an `AggregateStore` port with a Postgres bucket adapter now and a RocksDB/Redis adapter later; make the rule evaluator independent of the store so simulation replays Postgres history through identical code.
